blocks.prompt: 6 (i) Find \(y_{4}\) and write expressions for \(y_{10}\) and \(y_{11}\) without evaluating them: \(y = \sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan sine ke baar baar derivatives chahiye. 11 dafa differentiate karne ki bajaye pattern pehchanenge.
Diya kya hai? \(y = \sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\).
Find kya karna hai? \(y_{4}\) poora, aur \(y_{10}\), \(y_{11}\) sirf pattern se ("without evaluating").
Rule kaunsa? Chain rule; \(\sin\) ka derivative \(\cos\), \(\cos\) ka \(-\sin\).
Plan: \(y_{1}\) se \(y_{4}\) tak nikalo, dekho ke chaar qadam baad cycle dohraya jata hai, phir 10 aur 11 ko 4 se divide kar ke baqi dekho.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = \sin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\).
Maloom karna: \(y_{4}\), \(y_{10}\), \(y_{11}\).
Tareeqa: har dafa differentiate karne par chain rule ka \(\frac{1}{2}\) aata hai, aur function \(\sin \to \cos \to -\sin \to -\cos \to \sin\) ke chakkar mein ghoomta hai.

Pehle chaar derivatives
\[y_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\cos\dfrac{x}{2}\]
\[y_{2} = -\dfrac{1}{2^{2}}\sin\dfrac{x}{2}\]
\[y_{3} = -\dfrac{1}{2^{3}}\cos\dfrac{x}{2}\]
\[y_{4} = \dfrac{1}{2^{4}}\sin\dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{1}{16}\sin\dfrac{x}{2}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dx}\sin u = \cos u\frac{du}{dx}\) aur \(\frac{d}{dx}\cos u = -\sin u\frac{du}{dx}\), jahan \(u = \frac{x}{2}\), \(\frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}\). Har qadam par ek \(\frac{1}{2}\) aur multiply hota hai, is liye \(\frac{1}{2^{n}}\).
Dhyan dein: \(y_{3}\) mein \(-\sin\) ka derivative \(-\cos\) hai, aur \(y_{4}\) mein \(-\cos\) ka derivative \(+\sin\) (minus minus plus).

Pattern
\(y_{n}\) mein hamesha \(\frac{1}{2^{n}}\) hota hai; sign aur function har 4 qadam baad dohraye jate hain: \(n = 4k + 1\) par \(+\cos\); \(4k + 2\) par \(-\sin\); \(4k + 3\) par \(-\cos\); \(4k\) par \(+\sin\).
Kyun: chaar qadam ke baad hum wapas \(\sin\frac{x}{2}\) par aa jate hain, bilkul ghari ki suiyon ki tarah jo baarah ke baad phir ek se shuru hoti hain.

\(y_{10}\) aur \(y_{11}\)
\(10 = 4 \times 2 + 2\) aur \(11 = 4 \times 2 + 3\), is liye
\[y_{10} = -\dfrac{1}{2^{10}}\sin\dfrac{x}{2}\]
\[y_{11} = -\dfrac{1}{2^{11}}\cos\dfrac{x}{2}\]
Kyun: 10 ko 4 se divide karein to baqi 2, yani \(y_{10}\) ki shakal \(y_{2}\) jaisi; 11 ka baqi 3, yani \(y_{11}\) ki shakal \(y_{3}\) jaisi. Sirf \(\frac{1}{2}\) ki power badal kar 10 aur 11 ho gayi.

Tasdeeq
Ek hi formula: \(y_{n} = \frac{1}{2^{n}}\sin\left(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{n\pi}{2}\right)\), kyunke har derivative angle ko \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) aage kar deta hai. \(n = 10\): \(\sin\left(\frac{x}{2} + 5\pi\right) = -\sin\frac{x}{2}\); \(n = 11\): \(\sin\left(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{11\pi}{2}\right) = -\cos\frac{x}{2}\). Wohi jawab.

blocks.prompt: 6 (ii) Find \(y_{4}\) and write expressions for \(y_{10}\) and \(y_{11}\) without evaluating them: \(y = \ln(x^{2} - a^{2})\).
blocks.explanation:
Pehle logarithm ko todenge, bilkul Example 14 ki tarah; phir har term ek saada power ban jayegi.
Diya kya hai? \(y = \ln(x^{2} - a^{2})\).
Find kya karna hai? \(y_{4}\), aur pattern se \(y_{10}\), \(y_{11}\).
Rule kaunsa? \(\ln pq = \ln p + \ln q\), log ka derivative, power rule.
Plan: \(y = \ln(x - a) + \ln(x + a)\), chaar derivatives, coefficients mein factorial ka pattern, phir \(n = 10, 11\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = \ln(x^{2} - a^{2})\).
Maloom karna: \(y_{4}\), \(y_{10}\), \(y_{11}\).
Tareeqa: \(x^{2} - a^{2} = (x - a)(x + a)\) (do squares ka farq) aur log ka product law. Seedha differentiate karte to quotient rule baar baar lagta; todne se kaam bohat aasaan ho jata hai.

Logarithm ko todein
\[y = \ln(x - a) + \ln(x + a)\]
Kyun: \(\ln(pq) = \ln p + \ln q\). (Yeh \(x > a > 0\) ke liye hai; \(\ln|x - a| + \ln|x + a|\) lein to derivatives har jagah wohi aate hain.)

Pehle chaar derivatives
\[y_{1} = (x - a)^{-1} + (x + a)^{-1}\]
\[y_{2} = -(x - a)^{-2} - (x + a)^{-2}\]
\[y_{3} = 2(x - a)^{-3} + 2(x + a)^{-3}\]
\[y_{4} = -6(x - a)^{-4} - 6(x + a)^{-4}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln u = \frac{1}{u}\frac{du}{dx}\); \(x \pm a\) ka andar wala derivative 1 hai, is liye yahan koi extra factor nahi aata. Phir har dafa power rule: power aage aati hai aur ek kam hoti hai: \(-1\), phir \(-1 \times -2 = 2\), phir \(2 \times -3 = -6\).

Pattern
Coefficients \(1, -1, 2, -6\) asal mein \((-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!\) hain:
\[y_{n} = (-1)^{n-1}(n-1)!\;\times\]
\[\left[\dfrac{1}{(x - a)^{n}} + \dfrac{1}{(x + a)^{n}}\right]\]
Kyun: har qadam par negative power aage aati hai, is liye sign ek dafa plus ek dafa minus hota hai, aur size \(1, 1, 2, 6, 24, \ldots\) yani factorial ki tarah barhta hai.

Tasdeeq
Pattern \(n = 4\) par \((-1)^{3}\,3!\,[\ldots] = -6[\ldots]\) deta hai, jo seedhe hisaab se mil gaya. Formula sahi hai.
